Vājapeya
------------------------------------------
See VEDIC SACRIFICES for a short account.

vajra
------------------------------------------
This word has three meanings:
diamond;
the thunderbolt of the god इन्द्र;
lightning.
According to certain Āyurvedic texts, wearing a diamond on the body gives it firmness and also rejuvenates it.
It is of course used in various ornaments.
As regards its meaning as इन्द्र’s special weapon, see VAJRĀYUDHA.
Vajra, according to the Bhāgavata (1.15.39), was the great-grandson of Lord कृष्ण (son of अनिरुद्ध and Uṣā) who was installed as the king of the country known as शूरसेन. He was one of the five survivors after the Yādavas’ internecine fighting.

Vājasaneya Saṁhitā
------------------------------------------
See ŚUKLA यजुर्वेद SAṀHITĀ and YAJURVEDA.

Vajrāyudha
(‘the thunderbolt weapon’)
------------------------------------------
This is the invincible weapon of इन्द्र with which he killed many powerful असुरस् (demons) like Vṛtra.
It is said to have been shaped out of the backbone of the sage दधीचि (See DADHĪCI.) by विश्वकर्म, the architect of the gods.
